question:
**The following sentence has been split into segments. One of them may contain an error. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.**

No one were / present when I / entered the hall.
solution:
The erroneous part is** 'No one were'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here,** 'No one was' **should be used instead of **'No one were'.**
 
• ">The indefinite pronouns ">anyone, everyone, someone, no one, nobody "> are always singular and, therefore, require singular verbs.
 
 
• ">​E.X.- No one is interested in the game.
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is Option 2.

​Note- We use no one, nobody, nothing and nowhere to refer to an absence of people, things or places. We use them with a singular verb

**Correct Sentence:__** ***No one was** present when I entered the hall.*
